dashboard.purpose: Monitor a small, truthful set of operational signals and decide the next action.

entity-list.purpose: Browse and operate on comparable operational records such as customer, delivery, supply, finance, or service workstreams.

shell.selectionRule: Use AppShell when persistent workspace navigation and operational density are part of the task.

entity-detail.purpose: Read and act on one structured record without inventing a new data grammar.

entity-form.purpose: Create or edit one structured record through grouped, labelled ten4seven controls.

master-detail.purpose: Keep a record list visible while inspecting or updating one selected record.

approval-queue.purpose: Review, approve, reject, and safely bulk-operate on pending records.

settings.purpose: Edit application, workspace, or personal preferences.

report.purpose: Inspect a time-bounded result set and export a supported report.

catalog.purpose: Browse visual products, courses, books, or media with content-first composition.

shell.selectionRule: Use PublicShell for a public, content-first storefront; choose AppShell only when the catalog is inside a persistent authenticated workspace.

product-detail.purpose: Present one product with media, record context, price, and bounded purchase or save actions.

checkout.purpose: Collect the information needed to confirm an order without owning cart or payment business state.

content-list.purpose: Browse articles, lessons, documents, or media without forcing table semantics.

content-detail.purpose: Read one article, lesson, or document with clear metadata and bounded supporting actions.

ebook-reader.purpose: Read an ebook while preserving progress and reader controls.

auth.purpose: Sign in, register, recover access, or verify identity.

marketing-home.purpose: Explain a product through reusable expressive sections and drive one primary acquisition action.

shell.selectionRule: Use PublicShell for a public acquisition surface; keep block order and page-level actions in the recipe rather than rebuilding a shell locally.

cart.purpose: Review selected products, adjust bounded quantities, and continue to checkout without owning commerce persistence.

control-tower.purpose: Prioritize operational exceptions, accountable actions, current movement, and near-term sufficiency without turning the surface into a vanity KPI dashboard.

useWhen: the first question is what needs attention across several operational flows
owners need one place to see current movement, near-term risk, and next accountable actions
avoidWhen: the task is a historical analytics report
a single object's lifecycle is the primary subject
requiredSemantics: Forecast or capacity context when decision-relevant

responsive.desktop: Use an attention-first grid with signals and supporting context beside the queue.
responsive.tablet: Reduce supporting metrics before compressing the exception and action columns.
responsive.mobile: Stack critical exception, next action, current state, forecast, then supporting history.

accessibility: Expose one main heading and named regions for attention, forecast, and queue content.
State severity in text and iconography; never rely on color alone.
Keep exception actions keyboard reachable and restore focus after contextual inspection.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Control Tower when the user needs an operational overview whose hierarchy begins with exceptions and accountable actions, not generic totals.
antiPatterns: Leading with total orders, customers, or revenue when they do not change the next decision
Making every healthy signal bright green
Using a chart collection as a substitute for an exception queue

process-workspace.purpose: Explain and advance one operational object's lifecycle through explicit stage, progress, health, owner, evidence, and next-action semantics.

useWhen: one order, receipt, delivery, request, or case moves through a known lifecycle
the user must understand current ownership and the next checkpoint
avoidWhen: users are triaging many unrelated objects
the stages are merely categories rather than lifecycle checkpoints
requiredSemantics: Current stage distinct from percentage progress
Timestamp or age when timing matters

responsive.desktop: Use a horizontal milestone sequence with one active detail region.
responsive.tablet: Allow a bounded rail or an early vertical transition when labels stop scanning cleanly.
responsive.mobile: Use a compact vertical lifecycle or bounded horizontal rail without shrinking labels.

accessibility: Expose the lifecycle as a named navigation region or ordered sequence.
Mark the selected checkpoint with aria-current and keep its detail relationship explicit.
Announce progress numerically and describe blocked state in text.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Process Workspace for one object's lifecycle; choose Operational Kanban for a portfolio of objects waiting for people.
antiPatterns: Using Kanban columns to represent one object's lifecycle
Deriving health or severity from completion percentage
Hiding the current owner or next action

operational-kanban.purpose: Organize a portfolio of operational objects by work stage while preserving owner, age, next action, and exception visibility.

useWhen: people manage many work items waiting in human-action stages
stage balance, age, ownership, and WIP visibility drive daily coordination
avoidWhen: the surface follows one object's ordered lifecycle
stable cross-record comparison is better served by a DataTable

responsive.desktop: Use bounded stage columns with scan-first cards and visible column headings.
responsive.tablet: Allow horizontal board scrolling only when columns retain readable width.
responsive.mobile: Prefer a stage-by-stage stacked sequence or explicit stage switcher over miniature columns.

accessibility: Expose every column with a heading and count.
Preserve a logical DOM order independent of visual placement.
Do not make drag-and-drop the only way to change or inspect work.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Operational Kanban for many work items awaiting people; do not use it for the lifecycle of one object.
antiPatterns: Oversized decorative cards
Mouse-only drag behavior
Using color alone for stage or exception state

load-planning.purpose: Compose vehicle capacity, allocation, remaining space, utilization, manifest, sequence, and readiness without owning business thresholds.

useWhen: capacity constrains assignment or dispatch
users need to compare allocated and remaining quantity with a manifest
avoidWhen: the application has no capacity concept
a percentage alone is sufficient and no manifest or sequence exists

responsive.desktop: Place capacity summary beside manifest and route context.
responsive.tablet: Stack summary above the manifest while retaining table comparison.
responsive.mobile: Order content as summary, manifest, then route sequence; never shrink a planning canvas into unreadability.

accessibility: Give utilization a text label and numeric progress value.
Use table or list semantics for the manifest.
State readiness and exceptions in text, not only color.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Load Planning when capacity drives work; let the consumer supply operational targets and threshold meaning.
antiPatterns: Treating 80 percent utilization as universal success
Hiding absolute quantities behind a gauge
Creating domain-specific load-card primitives

receiving-console.purpose: Represent arrival, unloading, QC, receipt, and inventory as distinct states with explicit quantity discrepancies and decisions.

useWhen: physical arrival must remain distinct from accepted receipt and inventory posting
ordered, delivered, physical, accepted, rejected, or damaged quantities can diverge
avoidWhen: arrival and receipt are genuinely atomic in the consumer domain
the surface only needs a historical receipt record
requiredSemantics: Rejected, damaged, short, over, or mismatch state when present

responsive.desktop: Keep lifecycle and reconciliation visible beside the decision context.
responsive.tablet: Stack the lifecycle before quantities and decision controls.
responsive.mobile: Preserve arrival, current unloading, quantities, decision, and action in one vertical sequence.

accessibility: Announce receiving progress numerically.
Use explicit row labels for every quantity type.
Provide a labelled decision fieldset and descriptive action wording.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Receiving Console when physical handling, reconciliation, and QC separate arrival from receipt.
antiPatterns: Equating vehicle arrival with received inventory
Collapsing all quantities into one Quantity field
Using a generic confirmation dialog where evidence is required

route-planning.purpose: Present ordered stops, capacity, current state, ETA, completion, and exceptions while keeping map visualization optional.

useWhen: the order of operational stops matters
users need a route sequence even when map services are unavailable
avoidWhen: location order has no operational meaning
the request is for a routing optimization algorithm

responsive.desktop: Show route sequence beside or below capacity context; a map may support but not replace it.
responsive.tablet: Keep the ordered sequence readable before reducing supporting visualization.
responsive.mobile: Stack trip summary and ordered stops; keep sequence, ETA, quantity, and state visible.

accessibility: Use an ordered list or semantically ordered table for stops.
State current and completed checkpoints in text.
Do not require a visual map to understand the route.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Route Planning when sequence matters; treat maps as optional supporting visualization and never invent routing logic in the design system.
antiPatterns: Making a map the only representation of route order
Hiding ETA or quantity behind a hover interaction
Implementing route optimization inside Ten4Seven

entity-360.purpose: Compose one reusable business-partner workspace for customer, supplier, or farmer context without embedding domain scoring logic.

useWhen: users need one relationship view across current work, signals, activity, and history
customer, supplier, or farmer data shares the same structural anatomy
avoidWhen: the task is only a small contact card
the consumer expects Ten4Seven to calculate business reliability or scoring

responsive.desktop: Use summary, current work, and activity or detail in a clear multi-region composition.
responsive.tablet: Keep the entity summary first and collapse secondary history below current work.
responsive.mobile: Order summary, current work, signals, activity, then history.

accessibility: Use one entity heading and named sections for current work, signals, activity, and history.
Keep tables and timelines in logical reading order.
Provide text for relationship health and exceptions.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Entity 360 for shared customer, supplier, or farmer context; keep scoring and business rules consumer-owned.
antiPatterns: Creating structurally unrelated customer, supplier, and farmer shells
Embedding opaque business scores in the design system
Replacing current work with a profile-only card

decision-workspace.purpose: Put object context, evidence, impact, explicit options, reason, authority, and the consequential action in one accountable decision flow.

useWhen: a human must review evidence before approval, QC, verification, hold, rejection, or exception resolution
the consequence and reason must remain traceable
avoidWhen: the action is a simple reversible toggle
a short AlertDialog is sufficient after the user already has full context

responsive.desktop: Keep evidence and decision controls in one bounded workspace with one primary action.
responsive.tablet: Stack evidence before options without separating the reason from its action.
responsive.mobile: Preserve evidence, decision, reason, and action in one uninterrupted vertical sequence.

accessibility: Group mutually exclusive options in a labelled fieldset.
Associate the reason label with its textarea.
State consequences and submitted outcome in text.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Decision Workspace when judgment depends on evidence; use AlertDialog only as a final safeguard for an already-understood irreversible action.
antiPatterns: Reducing an evidence-led decision to Are you sure and OK
Communicating the selected outcome by color alone
Hiding consequence or required authority

exception-queue.purpose: Isolate work that requires attention and preserve its reason, severity, owner, age, and next action for fast operational triage.

useWhen: the primary question is which work requires attention
operators need comparable exception reason, age, owner, and next action
avoidWhen: normal and exceptional work should be browsed together
the task is a generic KPI dashboard

responsive.desktop: Use a comparable table or dense list with the action visible.
responsive.tablet: Retain columns that explain reason, owner, and next action; scroll or stack secondary context.
responsive.mobile: Use stacked record anatomy or controlled table scrolling without hiding the exception reason.

accessibility: Give the queue and table an accessible name.
State severity and reason in text.
Make row inspection keyboard operable and restore focus after the drawer closes.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Exception Queue when attention work is the primary collection; start from the canonical Entity List scaffold and omit irrelevant KPI or bulk controls.
antiPatterns: Mixing healthy records with exceptions at equal visual weight
Rendering giant red cards for every issue
Removing owner or next action from the queue

activity-audit.purpose: Compose readable operational activity and evidence-oriented audit history from the same trace foundation without treating the concepts as identical.

useWhen: users need a readable narrative of operational changes
evidence requires actor, timestamp, object, result, and state-change trace
avoidWhen: the surface is only a transient notification list
immutable audit requirements are being simulated without a consumer-owned evidence source

responsive.desktop: Keep a readable ordered feed beside current object context when useful.
responsive.tablet: Move the trace below current work while preserving event order.
responsive.mobile: Use one chronological column with actor, action, and timestamp kept together.

accessibility: Use ordered-list semantics for chronological narrative.
Keep timestamps and actor labels available as text.
Do not represent result only with color or icon.
operational.aiGuidance: Use ActivityFeed for readable activity; add evidence-oriented fields when the consumer is presenting an audit trail, and do not claim immutability from UI alone.
antiPatterns: Treating activity and audit as identical product concepts
Dropping actor or timestamp
Claiming immutable audit behavior from fixture presentation

resource-forecast.purpose: Communicate resource sufficiency through current quantity, consumption, days of cover, incoming supply, target context, and trend without implementing forecasting logic.

useWhen: an absolute stock quantity matters mainly through operational sufficiency
users need days of cover and incoming supply beside current consumption
avoidWhen: the consumer has no reliable consumption or incoming-supply calculation
the request is to implement a forecasting algorithm

responsive.desktop: Compose sufficiency as a compact decision signal within a Control Tower or resource view.
responsive.tablet: Keep quantity, days of cover, and incoming supply together before secondary trend detail.
responsive.mobile: Stack absolute quantity, time-to-empty, incoming supply, then trend without hiding units.

accessibility: Name quantity, unit, days of cover, and incoming ETA in text.
Give compact trends an accessible summary.
Do not rely on chart color to communicate sufficiency.
operational.aiGuidance: Choose Resource Forecast when sufficiency matters; Ten4Seven presents consumer-calculated values and does not predict them.
antiPatterns: Showing stock quantity without time-to-empty when sufficiency is the decision
Hiding incoming supply
Implementing forecasting or safety-stock algorithms in Ten4Seven
